_source: Hand-reviewed behavioral goldens for the two 'which sync session wins' decisions, shared by the native shells' copies: Swift SyncManager.hostedConnectEntry / SyncManager.restoreBranch (apps/ios/Sources/Sync/SyncManager.swift) and Kotlin SyncManager.hostedConnectEntry / SyncManager.restoreBranch (apps/android/.../SyncManager.kt). Each shell's unit test asserts its copy against these cases so the two cannot silently drift. Desktop has no copy: syncServiceE2ee's ensureConnected already prefers hosted and has no live-session teardown to sequence.
description: Justin's calls of 2026-09-16 (D8 + D9), specified in docs/spec/sync.md. hostedConnectEntry says what a hosted connect does about whatever session the manager is already holding; restoreBranch says which credential a cold launch reaches for.

hostedConnectEntry.description: D8. Inputs are the manager's own live state. 'skip' is the wizard's idempotent re-entry — it fires a connect whenever it sees an unlocked vault, and a second client would leave the first one's live loop running. 'replaceSelfHosted' is the switch: finishing hosted setup tears the self-hosted session down (a REAL teardown — Rust stops the live loop and demotes the vault) and then connects hosted. 'proceed' is an ordinary first connect. The guard is mode-aware precisely because a live password session used to satisfy it and silently skip the whole hosted connect.

cases.name: a first connect on a device holding nothing
the wizard re-entering on an already-hosted session
a hosted session being healed is rebuilt, not skipped
hosted setup finishing over a live self-hosted session
a self-hosted session mid-heal is still replaced
a self-hosted client whose last cycle failed still owns a live loop
connected hosted with no client left is not a session to skip for
a self-hosted session already torn down needs no second teardown

restoreBranch.description: D9. What a cold launch reaches for, from two local secret-store reads and no network. Holding BOTH is the one ambiguous state, and it resolves to hosted: it can only be a device stranded by a build from before a hosted connect cleared the password, because both shells stop offering the self-hosted fields once hosted sync is set up. The hosted connect then clears the password, so the state cannot recur and the branch retires itself. This is NOT a general inversion of the precedence — with no hosted vault the password still wins, which is what keeps a self-hosted device self-hosted.

cases.name: a device that has never synced
a self-hosted device reconnects to its own server
a hosted device resumes its hosted session
a device stranded holding both resumes hosted and heals
